issues.body:
## Problem

The v0.18.0 external-task completion contract requires `delivery.schema_validation.outcome: passed` and `exit_code: 0` inside the same file that the declared CLI validator must read. During the final downstream PR13 audit, the audit itself and its lifecycle schema passed, but automatic approval review rejected creating this self-declaring completion file before the CLI had executed.

The exact candidate also passed the canonical mapping validators in memory. Persisting those verified bytes was rejected again because the embedded external CLI result was still prospective. Both rejections remain non-passing delivery evidence; they do not erase the completed content audit.

## Required outcome

- Separate a draft completion payload from its independently produced validation receipt, or provide an equivalent non-circular validation interface.
- Make actual validation order explicit. No persisted draft may claim an unexecuted command passed; no final callback may be admitted without actual validation bound to the exact payload bytes.
- Retain truthful blocked, interrupted, and failed delivery records, and permit safe custody release without requiring a successful acceptance result.
- Review the design and add narrow regression coverage for the bootstrap, exact-byte binding, post-validation mutation, and blocked delivery cases before integration. Avoid rerunning unrelated package or downstream test matrices.

This follow-up does not modify the published v0.18.0 tag or assets. Any one-time downstream closeout exception remains a separate explicit owner decision.
issues.title: Remove circular pass assertion from external task completion validation

issues.body:
## Problem and desired outcome

Schema evolution across execution packets, completion records, validation receipts, templates, and instructions requires repeated manual synchronization. Agents currently construct YAML, canonical serialization, digests, and lease transitions during delivery. Format errors can stop useful work before behavioral verification starts, consuming time and model tokens.

Provide a small deterministic toolchain for constructing and evolving these artifacts. Agents should supply task intent and actual observations; tools should handle representation, versioning, and mechanical synchronization. Reduce existing maintenance surfaces rather than adding another parallel framework.

## Observed evidence

- Related repair: #310 and PR #311. Reference inspection used commit `b9da4e760d15c2d4d85a2a22064567ba83f7d001`; this is historical inspection context, not a claim about the eventual merged head.
- `.ai/scripts/validate-agent-execution-guardrails.py` defines packet and nested allowed fields directly in Python while `.ai/assets/shared/agent-execution-guardrails.schema.yaml` holds another portion of the contract.
- `validate-external-task-delegation.py` under the orchestrator skill separately embeds schema version, transport semantics, and receipt construction. It already has `--write-receipt`, so reuse/consolidate existing functionality.
- An audit attempt in the PR #311 work stopped before behavioral review because subject and criteria were supplied in dispatch prose but not in the sealed packet. This is an observed preparation failure, not proof that the implementation was correct or that every earlier audit was unnecessary.
- `.ai/scripts/generate-runtime-skill-entries.py` already demonstrates deterministic generation plus a read-only `--check` mode.

## Bounded scope

1. Start with execution packet and external-task dispatch/completion/receipt contracts. Inventory required consumers before choosing the smallest authoritative model; avoid a repository-wide schema rewrite.
2. Keep structural fields, types, versions, defaults, and field documentation in one maintained source. Generate templates and reference sections or load the same model directly. Keep behavioral checks in a shared implementation rather than copying them into prose and multiple validators.
3. Provide deterministic construction and finalization commands for required artifacts. Obtain Git identity and execution results from actual observations. Own canonical serialization, hashes, contained paths, and required lifecycle transitions in code.
4. Provide explicit version-aware compatibility or migrations with previewable output. Preserve historical artifacts and outcomes; request genuinely missing semantic inputs rather than inventing them or relabeling old evidence as newly executed.
5. Consolidate diagnostics behind one entry point that reports all detected input problems in one run and identifies a concrete repair action. Retire redundant code paths with an explicit compatibility plan.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One representative compatible and one incompatible contract change update all selected generated consumers deterministically; a second generation run produces no diff.
- [ ] The normal selected packet/completion/receipt workflow requires no agent-written hashes or hand-authored record envelopes.
- [ ] Receipt creation records actual validator/execution outcomes. Builders cannot manufacture a successful execution result from a default or migration.
- [ ] Supported historical inputs remain readable under declared version semantics; unsupported changes receive actionable diagnostics and never silently rewrite sealed history.
- [ ] A regression reproducing the PR #311 packet-preparation mismatch is diagnosed before dispatch, without running a behavioral audit just to discover malformed input.
- [ ] Independent behavioral tests cover outcome preservation, content mismatch, invalid paths, and version transitions; generated output passing a matching generated checker alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Report before/after manual edits, process invocations, and format-only failed attempts for a bounded comparable exercise. Report elapsed time and tokens only when actually observed; no assumed savings.
- [ ] Identify which old templates, duplicated checks, and manual instruction steps were removed or delegated to the common tool.

## Coordination and authorization

The owner explicitly requested online issues and a separate primary task on 2026-09-20. Authorized now: tracking, context preservation, read-only assessment, and a sequencing recommendation. Implementation timing is still being evaluated; creating this issue does not authorize editing the active PR #311 branch, interrupting its task, changing release/provider state, or merging either delivery.

Use an isolated worktree for assessment. Re-read PR #311 and current main before implementation. Prefer building on the integrated #310 repair; if the current work cannot reach a bounded checkpoint, report the concrete dependency and intervention option to the owner. Do not wait indefinitely for the unrelated #309 credential boundary.

Related: #313 (proportional terminal-gate requirements), #310 (current correctness repair), #307 (pre-tag execution reuse), #308 (validation input planning). Release, priority, and Project fields remain unassigned. Coordinate with #313 so automation does not merely preserve unnecessary ceremony.

issues.title: Standardize schema, execution-packet, and receipt generation and migration tooling

issues.body:
## Problem and desired outcome

The framework has reduced routine execution overhead but retains an extensive terminal path for merge and Issue closure. Format preparation can block behavioral review, and repeated preparation/retry work obscures whether each gate reduces an actual delivery risk. Standardized tooling should be accompanied by a focused review of which evidence requirements are necessary.

Make ordinary source merge/closure proportional to the risk and changes involved. Keep meaningful tests, review, outcome truthfulness, and verification of the actual integrated or published artifacts. Remove requirements whose only purpose is satisfying another bookkeeping layer.

## Evidence and limits

- Commit `45222964a2234744b0c7c7fef5add8725f985a1a` changed independent-review validity from commit identity alone to content identity with rebinding.
- Commit `6529159b16efada765b0646b831332a9065a4e67` reduced routine packet/lease overhead while explicitly retaining the full terminal/high-risk path.
- In the PR #311 work, audit attempt 008 produced no behavioral review conclusion because the sealed packet lacked subject/criteria that appeared in dispatch prose. Subsequent work prepared another packet for the same content. Earlier audit rounds also found genuine defects; their outcomes must not be dismissed as format-only failures.
- This is evidence of a workflow-cost problem. No aggregate false-block rate, elapsed-time savings, or token savings has yet been measured.

## Bounded assessment and proposed change scope

1. Trace only the selected source merge/closure route through AGENTS, terminal-closure policy, auditor role/runtime entry, guardrails, and their executable checks.
2. For each requirement, identify the concrete failure prevented, its evidence consumer, existing equivalent checks, and the cost of preparation or retry.
3. Distinguish genuine implementation defects, changed review content, missing execution facts, environmental failures, and representation-only preparation failures. Describe when to repair input, reuse still-valid results, rerun affected checks, or stop.
4. Define an implementable smaller path for ordinary merge/closure and explicit criteria for genuinely high-risk release or cross-boundary operations. Avoid automatic escalation to the heaviest evidence mode merely because a task is ending.
5. Align policy, role instructions, templates, and executable requirements together. Renaming fixed-head terminology alone does not satisfy this issue.
6. Coordinate with #312 (schema/receipt tooling); remove unnecessary requirements before automating their remaining mechanics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A concise disposition identifies each examined gate as retain, simplify, combine, or remove, with a concrete risk and affected consumers.
- [ ] Ordinary review input is checked once before dispatch; a formatting repair does not masquerade as a product defect or independently justify repeating unaffected behavioral checks.
- [ ] Unchanged content/criteria can retain valid review evidence under the accepted binding policy; changed behavior receives appropriately scoped fresh checks.
- [ ] Failed, missing, or unexecuted checks are never converted to passes, and release artifacts still correspond to the version actually verified.
- [ ] Ordinary and genuinely high-risk examples demonstrate the intended routing; policy and executable behavior agree.
- [ ] A bounded before/after exercise records avoided manual operations and format-only retries; timing/token claims use actual observations.
- [ ] Existing #307 and #308 remain owners of their specific release-reuse and input-resolution work; this issue does not duplicate their implementations.

## Coordination and authorization

On 2026-09-20 the owner requested durable online issues, a new primary task, and an assessment of whether to interrupt the active work. Authorized now: issue creation, context preservation, and read-only assessment. Do not interrupt the active task, waive PR #311 gates, modify its branch, assign release/priority/Project fields, or implement policy changes solely because this issue exists.

Initial sequencing recommendation: allow the active #310 correctness repair to reach a safe checkpoint while the new task assesses in an isolated checkout. Prefer a separate subsequent delivery after PR #311 integration. If continued work is blocked only by representation churn, present a bounded checkpoint/intervention recommendation instead of allowing an open-ended retry loop. The unrelated #309 credential requirement is not a prerequisite for this assessment.

Related: #310 and PR #311; #307; #308. No release allocation or completion claim is made.

issues.body:
## Problem

The current pre-tag interface always executes the complete release profile on integrated main. It also does so when the release profile already passed before a lifecycle-only transition, all affected checks passed afterward, independent review and hosted admission passed, and the merge commit has exactly the reviewed tree. The current contracts offer no acceptance path for that combined evidence.

This is separate from the fixture I/O measurement in #275. Broad release-record dependency declarations also cause lifecycle-only updates to select checks that may not consume the changed fields; those declarations need their own evidence-based review.

## Proposed scope

- Define a source-only integrated-release acceptance path in the source-release policy and pre-tag interface.
- Preserve the original profile execution subject and outcome. Do not label composed acceptance as a new release-profile pass or a cache hit.
- Require actual passed profile completion, explicit lease release, exact lifecycle-only comparison, freshly passed affected checks, independent audit, exact merged-tree equality, and fresh candidate, asset, hosted and provider admission evidence.
- Keep unknown dependencies, content or authority drift, environment-sensitive evidence and failed execution fail-closed.
- Evaluate narrower release lifecycle dependency declarations separately; packaged registry changes require normal new-candidate validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The unchanged-tree path proves every required acceptance has current, appropriately scoped evidence.
- [ ] Content, criteria, authority, command, environment or provider drift selects the applicable fresh checks or blocks acceptance.
- [ ] Missing, failed, interrupted and tampered evidence never produces accepted publication.
- [ ] Reports distinguish original execution, fresh affected checks and composed acceptance without inventing profile reuse.
- [ ] Measured avoided work is reported from real comparable runs; no credit or time savings are assumed.

## Allocation and authority

Follow-up to #302, unassigned to a release. This records a concrete issue found during v0.18.0 preparation. It does not change the frozen v0.18.0 candidate, waive its gates or claim implementation has occurred.

issues.body:
# Clarify optional validation input planning and unsupported gate diagnostics

The source resolver and normal evidence preparation interpret declared registry inputs differently. This was observed while preparing the v0.18.0 source release at e60ce278b7bef2674806fe631377396eb49b3447.

- `check-all.sh --resolve-input-closure` materializes every token with `git ls-tree` and rejects a zero-match token. `.git`, optional missing inputs, and some glob selectors therefore cannot use that interface.
- Normal evidence preparation fingerprints `.git` separately and represents unmatched selectors without treating them as execution failures.
- The optional `validation-evidence.py subject-manifest --gate-id ...` interface can accept a gate ID before discovering that its inputs or reuse eligibility are unsupported.
- The changed-path ownership matcher recognizes `**`, `?`, and `[` but not a single `*`, although registry selectors include single-star patterns.

Ordinary profile execution and the current eligible subject-rebind pilot were not found to depend on these unsupported cases. This is an input-planning/diagnostic limitation; it is not evidence that normal downstream validation fails. No downstream runtime reproduction is claimed.

Proposed bounded follow-up:

- Reject ineligible subject-manifest gates early with an explicit supported-input explanation, or deliberately represent their non-file/missing-selector semantics without granting reuse.
- Align wildcard ownership with the registry's intended selector semantics, preserving conservative selection and unknown-impact fallback.
- Cover missing optional inputs, creation/deletion/rename, single-star patterns, and history-sensitive gates with focused contracts.

Keep identity-sensitive gates fresh-required and retain failure on unknown authority. This issue does not allocate work to v0.18.0 or reopen its admitted package payload.
